method: Existing hit strength and 220 ms decay drive a bounded actor-frame rotation, distributed over three spine joints. Restore base before locomotion, then apply hit. Exact quaternion powers avoid small-angle nlerp bias.

performance_acceptance.scope: Finite real gameplay sample on the current Intel D3D11 device; assesses sustained low frame rate, not a guarantee of zero dropped frames.
performance_acceptance.definition: This run's finite DEV acceptance criteria, recorded after inspecting the sample; not a previously agreed or universal performance target.
performance_acceptance.known_observation: High quality had one 33.3 ms frame during turning among 623 frames; retain this observation rather than rerunning to select a cleaner sample.

gates: True engine hit produces a visible bounded reaction and returns to base
Pause, duplicate frame, round reset and death do not accumulate transforms
Real skinned shoes, hands, bone hierarchy and local positions/scales remain invariant
Before/after moving and stationary visual inspection
Full Vitest, CS Chromium, build and isolated five-bot gameplay performance

rejected.reason: Full aiming angles caused excessive torso bending. Runtime hit API has no aim channel. Shoulder/arm aim remains a separate task.

remaining: Shoulder/arm aim and limited head follow
Directional locomotion, turns and start/stop transitions
Existing finger grip and clothing/model quality
